explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The people gathered in such large numbers that there was "…no more room, not even outside the door…" (Mark 2:2) I've seen a full cookie jar, but that crowd had it beat. And Jesus is right in the middle of it, speaking the word to them.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says the people "…gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door…" (Mark 2:2) So there was no room left, even outside the door. And Jesus was speaking the word to them.

explanations.answer: Open the roof and lower him down on his mat
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend! They were unable to get through the crowd, so "…they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat." (Mark 2:4) When the front door is blocked, these four go for the ceiling. I admire that kind of stubborn.

explanations.answer: Wait outside until the whole crowd heads home
explanations.explanation: I get it, waiting is the polite move. But the text says they were unable to get through the crowd, so they "…uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat." (Mark 2:4) These four weren't waiting on anybody. They found another way in.

explanations.answer: Shout over the crowd for Jesus to come out
explanations.explanation: That would be a loud plan, friend, and I respect a loud plan. But the text never has them shouting. They "…uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat." (Mark 2:4) They took the man to Jesus instead of calling Jesus out to him.

explanations.answer: faith
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" (Mark 2:5) The text says their faith, and Jesus saw it. Then He spoke to the man on the mat.

explanations.answer: fear
explanations.explanation: Fear makes sense when you're ripping up a roof, friend. I'd be nervous about the homeowner. But the text says "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" (Mark 2:5) What Jesus saw was their faith.

explanations.answer: pride
explanations.explanation: Nope, friend. Nothing in the text points to pride. It says "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" (Mark 2:5) Faith is what Jesus saw.

explanations.answer: Son your sins are forgiven
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Jesus says, "Son, your sins are forgiven." (Mark 2:5) I bet a few people in that house expected something else first. Jesus starts with forgiveness, and He says it right to the man on the mat.

explanations.answer: Son go show yourself to the priest
explanations.explanation: That's not what Jesus says here, friend. In Mark 2:5 He says, "Son, your sins are forgiven." Nothing about a priest shows up in His words. He starts with forgiveness.

explanations.answer: Son your faith has healed you
explanations.explanation: That one sounds so much like Jesus that I almost picked it myself. But here He says, "Son, your sins are forgiven." (Mark 2:5) Those words come first, and the man hasn't been told to stand yet.

explanations.answer: He is blaspheming since only God can forgive sins
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The scribes are thinking in their hearts, "Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:6-7) Their question is a good one, and Jesus is about to answer it.

explanations.answer: He should not be teaching on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: Fair guess, friend, but that's not in this passage. The scribes think, "He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:7) The Sabbath isn't mentioned here, and what they're thinking is about forgiveness.

explanations.answer: He should have healed the man before anything else
explanations.explanation: Plenty of folks in that room might have wanted that, friend. But the scribes aren't complaining about the order. They're thinking, "He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:7) The forgiveness is what bothers them.

explanations.answer: He knows it in His spirit
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend, He knew it in His spirit. "At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves." (Mark 2:8) Nobody had to tell Him anything, because He knew it right away. Then He asked them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?" (Mark 2:8)

explanations.answer: A man in the crowd tells Him
explanations.explanation: In a house that packed, I could see somebody leaning over to whisper. But the text says "At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves." (Mark 2:8) No messenger, no tip. He knew it in His spirit.

explanations.answer: He guesses it from their silence
explanations.explanation: Silence can say a lot, friend, but this wasn't a guess. "At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves." (Mark 2:8) The text says He knew it, not that He guessed. He knew it right away, and He knew it in His spirit.

explanations.answer: So they know He has authority to forgive sins
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker! Jesus says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins..." (Mark 2:10) "…Son of Man…" is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So the reason He gives is His authority to forgive sins.

explanations.answer: So they know He is a prophet like Elijah
explanations.explanation: Elijah is a fine name to know, friend, but Jesus doesn't say it here. He says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins..." (Mark 2:10) The point is His authority to forgive.

explanations.answer: So they know God has heard the man's prayers
explanations.explanation: That's a kind thought, friend, but the text never mentions the man praying. Jesus says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." (Mark 2:10) The reason He gives is His authority to forgive.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. Jesus says, "I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home." and the man "immediately" got up. (Mark 2:11-12) Nobody had to help him stand. The man went from the mat to his feet right away.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Right, friend, it's False. "…immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all." (Mark 2:12) The text says nothing about waiting or a helping hand. I'd have needed a minute and a cookie, but he stood right up.

explanations.answer: astounded
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says "…they were all astounded…" (Mark 2:12) The man walked out in front of them all. And they said, "We have never seen anything like this!"

explanations.answer: glorified
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. "…they were all astounded and glorified God…" (Mark 2:12) What they saw sent their praise to God. And they said, "We have never seen anything like this!"

explanations.answer: frightened
explanations.explanation: I can see why you'd pick it, friend. A man walking out on his own is a lot to take in. But the text says they "…were all astounded and glorified God…" (Mark 2:12) It doesn't say they were frightened.

explanations.answer: questioned
explanations.explanation: The scribes were asking questions in their hearts earlier, so I see where this comes from. But at the end, the text says they "…were all astounded and glorified God…" (Mark 2:12) The questioning part doesn't show up in that line.

explanations.answer: doubted
explanations.explanation: Not this one, friend. The text says "…they were all astounded and glorified God…" (Mark 2:12) It doesn't say they doubted. After the man walked out in front of them all, what the text says is astounded and glorified God.
